entry.title: Geese Earn First Grammy Nominations
entry.summary: Including Best New Artist and Best Alternative Music Album
entry.content:
Could a psyop do this? Geese have received their first-ever Grammy nominations, bringing in five nods total. The indie rockers are up for Best New Artist, Best Alternative Music Album (for Getting Killed), Best Rock Performance and Best Rock Song (for “Trinidad”), and Best Alternative Music Performance (for “Au Pays du Cocaine”).

The New York band will duke it out in the Best New Artist category against polka-dotted math rockers Angine de Poitrine, pop phenom Slayyyter, country star Ella Langley, and rapper Don Toliver. They’re also going head to head with Angine de Poitrine for Best Rock Performance and Best Alternative Music Performance. Rounding out the former category are the Rolling Stones, Phoebe Bridgers, and Olivia Rodrigo and Robert Smith for their duet “What’s Wrong With Me.” The latter category includes Bridgers, Rosalía, and Hayley Williams.

Geese’s nominations cap off a breakout year for the quartet of Cameron Winter, Max Bassin, Emily Green, and Dominic DiGesu, who have spent much of 2026 touring behind Getting Killed. They made their Saturday Night Live debut back in January, and won International Group of the Year at the BRIT Awards in February. They also released a live album, Live at Third Man Records, in March.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place in Los Angeles on Sunday, February 7 at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT. You can watch along from home via ABC, Disney+, and Hulu, all three of which will provide live coverage of music’s biggest night.

Follow along with all of Pitchfork’s Grammys 2027 coverage.

entry.title: Angine de Poitrine Nominated for Best New Artist at 2027 Grammys
entry.summary: They’re up against Geese, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, the Womack Sisters, Ella Langley, and Remi Wold
entry.content:
The 2027 Grammy Award nominations are here, which means the Best New Artist race is upon us. This year’s spread, delightfully, includes Montréal microtonal duo (trio?) Angine de Poitrine, known for their outlandish spotted attire and math rock riffs. They’ll face off against Slayyyter, Geese, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Ella Langley, Remi Wolf, and the Womack Sisters.

Angine de Poitrine are currently wrapping up a run of live dates through North America. They’ll then power down for a few months before heading out on a 2027 international trek.

Find out who else is nominated this year here.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers, Charli XCX, Rosalía, and Geese Face Off for Best Alternative Album Grammy
entry.summary: Alabama Shakes and Gorillaz are also nominated in the category
entry.content:
Nominations for Best Alternative Music Album have been unveiled for the 2027 Grammy Awards. Facing off in the illustrious but ill-defined category are Alabama Shakes (I Must Be Dreaming), Phoebe Bridgers (Lost Weekend), Charli XCX (Music, Fashion, Film), Geese (Getting Killed), Gorillaz (The Mountain), and, for Lux (Complete Works), Rosalía. That is: anything cool that does not obviously fit anywhere else. Many of these artists look set for a big year: Bridgers, Geese, and Rosalía have already picked up multiple nods elsewhere, too.

The 2026 victors in the category were the Cure, who secured their first-ever statuettes this year, for Songs of a Lost World and its single “Alone.”

Follow along with all of Pitchfork’s Grammys 2027 coverage.

entry.title: Tinashe, Slayyyter, Underscores Are Officially Grammy Nominees
entry.summary: The first-time hopefuls will face off in the Best Dance/Electronic Recording category
entry.content:
The Best Dance/Electronic Recording category is in surprisingly good shape at the 2027 Grammy Awards, with Slayyyter, Underscores, and—somehow—Tinashe picking up their first-ever nominations. Recognized for “Crank,” “Music,” and “Melatonin,” respectively, the three first-timers are up against Madonna (“I Feel So Free”), Fred Again.. and Jamie T (“Lights Burn Dimmer”), and Tame Impala (“My Old Ways”). Both Tinashe and Slayyyter are also up for Best Dance Pop Recording; Slayyyter will also compete for Best New Artist and Best Dance/Electronic Album. As ever, the Recording Academy’s common-sense committee can’t win ’em all: Popstar did not receive nods in any album categories.

The nominations cap banner years for all three artists, including the fast-rising Underscores, who was vaulted into arenas in support of Charli XCX. A Slayyyter run behind Wor$t Girl in America, meanwhile, took her to Madison Square Garden.

Read Walden Green’s profile Saint Slayyyter, Kieran Press-Reynolds’ The Not-So-Secret History of Underscores, and follow along with all of Pitchfork’s Grammys 2027 coverage.

entry.title: Grammy Nominations 2027: See the Full List Here
entry.summary: Find out who’s up for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, Best New Artist, and more
entry.content:
The 2027 Grammy Awards are coming up fast, and today (November 16), the Recording Academy announced which artists are in the running for trophies. Leading the pack this year is Raye, whose count of 11 nominations—among them the trifecta of Album, Song, and Record of the Year—ties Beyonce’s 2025 record for the most nominations for a female artist in one year. Close behind is Rosalía with nine nominations behind her 2025 album Lux; she is a first-time nominee in every category she’s up for this year, including Record and Song of the Year. Ella Langley, whose smash “Choosing Texas” became the longest-running No. 1 on the Hot 100 in history this year, has seven nominations, which ties her with her “Choosin Texas’’ co-songwriter Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo, and Phoebe Bridgers.

The Album of the Year race features Bridgers’ Lost Weekend, Rodrigo’s You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love, Langley’s Dandelion, Rosalía’s Lux, and Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl; rounding out the top-line category are Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope, Olivia Dean’s The Art of Loving, and Bruno Mars’ The Romantic. Many of those artists double up in Song of the Year: Bridgers’ “Lost Boys,” Rodrigo’s “The Cure,” Raye’s “Where Is My Husband?,” Mars’ “Risk It All,” Rosalía’s “Berghain,” and Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” are all represented, while Ariana Grande picked up a nod for her Petal lead single “Hate That I Made You Love Me.” Swift is in the running, too—not for a TLOAS track, but for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” her original song for Toy Story 5. It’s also up for Best Song Written for Visual Media, a category that includes Andrew Bird’s single for The Pitt and Charli XCX and John Cale’s Wuthering Heights track “House.”

It’s also shaping up to be a big year for first-time nominees. Underscores picked up a nod for Best Dance/Electronic Recording, and Slayyyter and Tinashe both received nominations in the same category, as well as Best Dance Pop Recording. Slayyyter is also nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Album for Wor$t Girl in America. On the other end of the spectrum, Madonna brought her career nominations to 32 with four nominations for Confessions II. The original Confessions on a Dance Floor won Best Electronic/Dance Album Category at the 2007 Grammys.

Next year’s show marks the first time Disney+ will air the event, taking over for longtime host CBS. It will also air live on ABC and Hulu as part of the partnership. Winners will be announced during the ceremony on Sunday, February 7 at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT.

Last year’s Grammys saw big wins for Bad Bunny, Lady Gaga, Clipse, the Cure, Nine Inch Nails, and FKA twigs, plus an all-star tribute to the late Ozzy Osbourne. A number of winners also took the opportunity to protest the actions of ICE. Joni Mitchell wore an ICE Out pin while accepting Best Historical Recording during the pre-show, and Olivia Dean showed love to her immigrant grandmother in her Best New Artist acceptance speech. Bad Bunny, accepting Best Música Urbana Album for eventual Album of the Year winner Debí Tirar Más Fotos, didn’t mince words, saying, “Before I say thanks to God, I’m going to say ICE out. We are not savage, we are not animals, we are not aliens, we are humans, and we are Americans.”

entry.title: Watch Phoebe Bridgers Play “Bobby” and “Still Standing” on Saturday Night Live
entry.summary: The singer-songwriter made her third SNL appearance, this time to promote Lost Weekend
entry.content:
A lot has changed since Phoebe Bridgers’ stint as a guitar-smashing musical guest on Saturday Night Live in 2021, notably her arena-headlining status as a solo act and another SNL appearance with the Grammy-dominating supergroup Boygenius. Last night (November 14), Bridgers visited Saturday Night Live yet again, this time to perform two songs from Lost Weekend: “Bobby” and “Still Standing.” Watch a replay below.

Joining Bridgers for the live rendition of “Bobby” was a full backing band, including Melina Duterte of Jay Som on guitar, and an eerie pooling of smoke by their feet. During “Still Standing,” Bridgers performed onstage alone in a white lace dress and simple makeup — normally unremarkable, except that during the final stretch of the song, black lights revealed she was actually wearing skeleton face paint.

Bridgers heads to Europe next month to continue her shows in support of Lost Weekend. She recently announced that tour is getting extended through 2027, including a bunch of new dates in North America with Paper Wings and her longtime collaborator Christian Lee Hutson.

Last month, Bridgers dropped a Tidal-exclusive live EP of songs from her new album, as recorded at Madison Square Garden. She’s also kept quite busy as an actor, starring in a nuanced role in Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime (for which she also chipped in an original song) and voice acting roles in short films by My Chemical Romance and Conor Oberst.

Read Hattie Lindert’s concert review Going Analog at Phoebe Bridgers’ Phones-Free MSG Show.

entry.title: Peter Hook, Lauren Mayberry, Deftones Play Joy Division and New Order Songs at 2026 Rock Hall
entry.summary: They christened the 2026 induction ceremony with “Love Will Tear Us Apart” and “Bizarre Love Triangle”
entry.content:
Last night (November 14), the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 induction ceremony took place at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, where Joy Division and New Order were simultaneously honored, with Trent Reznor handling their induction speech. Given the band members’ decades-long feud, only Hook showed up to the event. He was joined by Deftones to perform Joy Division’s eternal hit “Love Will Tear Us Apart,” with Chino Moreno handling lead vocals, and then Chvrches’ Lauren Mayberry took over on the mic for New Order’s “Bizarre Love Triangle.” Watch footage of their performance below.

“I’m on my own, but I’m not alone,” Hook said during his acceptance speech on behalf of both bands. “For me, it’s been a wild 50 years. I’ve been happy, I’ve been mad, I’ve been heartbroken in equal measures, but I’m still fucking here. Music is eternal, fans are eternal, and we are eternally grateful.” Hook did not mention his former bandmates by name at any point or thank them, apart from Joy Division’s late singer, Ian Curtis.

Joy Division and New Order are, of course, two different bands, but they were nominated as a package deal twice in the past, in 2023 and 2025, before earning the official selection in 2026. Their bundling makes sense considering Joy Division’s surviving members formed New Order after Curtis died in 1980. Hook’s beef with New Order is infamous. He left the band in 2007 and then spent years in a legal battle over royalties with his former bandmates. He previously said he wouldn’t appear at the induction ceremony’s podium with the group unless they apologized to him, and that he would be willing to perform together again if they did. Looks like the reunion bets are off.

This year, the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony was not live streamed. Instead, fans can tune in to watch a broadcast of the event on ABC and Disney+ on December 8. This other 2026 inductees were Oasis, Phil Collins, Iron Maiden, Wu-Tang Clan, Sade, Billy Idol, and Luther Vandross. The Early Influence Award was handed out to Fela Kuti, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, and Gram Parsons this year. Meanwhile, the Musical Excellence Awards went to Linda Creed and Rick Rubin, among others, while the late Ed Sullivan honored with the 2026 Ahmet Ertegun Award for non-artists.

entry.title: Watch Wu-Tang Clan Perform at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 Induction Ceremony
entry.summary: RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, and co. broke out the hits for the occasion
entry.content:
The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 induction ceremony took place last night (November 14), and Wu-Tang Clan were there to triumph. RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, Inspectah Deck, Cappadonna, and the rest of the crew were there for the honor, accepting the award from Chris Rock and performing “C.R.E.A.M. (Cash Rules Everything Around Me)” and “Shimmy Shimmy Ya” onstage together. Watch footage from the event below.

Everyone in Wu-Tang Clan took turns trading off during their acceptance speech, celebrating their status with plenty of bravado. RZA kicked things off with general appreciation (“It’s a testament to not only be recognized by our fans, but by the industry and other genres”) before others took over the microphone. “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” said Method Man. “I want to thank everyone who believed in us, and to anyone who didn’t, you can kiss my inducted ass.”

Wu-Tang Clan are the 16th hip-hop act to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, following in the footsteps of Notorious B.I.G., A Tribe Called Quest, and Missy Elliott. The New York collective were honored as a milestone in the genre for their use of storytelling, lo-fi beats, conversational interludes, philosophy, and martial arts references, thanks in large part to their debut album, 1993’s Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers).

This year, the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony was not live streamed. Instead, fans can tune in to watch a broadcast of the event on ABC and Disney+ on December 8. This year’s other inductees were Oasis, Phil Collins, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Sade, Billy Idol, and Luther Vandross. The Early Influence Award was handed out to Fela Kuti, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, and Gram Parsons this year. Meanwhile, the Musical Excellence Awards went to Linda Creed and Rick Rubin, among others, while the late Ed Sullivan honored with the 2026 Ahmet Ertegun Award for non-artists.

entry.title: Phil Collins Gets Rare Two-Time Inductee Status at Rock & Roll Hall of Fame
entry.summary: The Genesis musician was celebrated for his solo career at the 2026 Induction Ceremony
entry.content:
Phil Collins was one of the few honored artists to show up in person for the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 induction ceremony last night (November 14), and he seemed as happy as ever to be there. Collins is one of the rare two-time inductees at the Rock Hall thanks to Genesis’ recognition in 2010. For the occasion, he was introduced by fellow drum obsessive Travis Barker of Blink-182 and was serenaded to by Cynthia Erivo. Watch footage from the event below.

During his acceptance speech, Collins nodded to his status as the 29th individual to earn two inductions into the storied Rock Hall with humility, having welled up offstage during Barker’s essay. Collins also addressed his health as he took the stage using two crutches (“I’m really not as bad as it looks”), thanked his longtime manager and friends in music in music like Robert Plant and Eric Clapton (“[You] saw something that was worth nurturing”), and credited his path to fame as being sheer luck following his interest in drums as a kid (“Everything else has been a really happy accident”). Much to the crowd’s enthusiasm, Collins also revealed that the rumors of him retiring from touring or live performances isn’t true. “You haven't heard the last of me,” he said to cheers. “I can promise you that.”

It’s a no-brainer why Collins was inducted twice, especially considering he’s one of three artists to sell 100 million albums as both a member of a group and as a solo artist. He launched his solo career with 1981’s Face Value, featuring the all-timer single “In the Air Tonight,” and the rest was history: Hello, I Must Be Going!, No Jacket Required, …But Seriously, and beyond.

entry.title: Watch St. Vincent, Metallica, More Cover Iron Maiden at Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 Induction Ceremony
entry.summary: Rage Against the Machine’s Brad Wilk, Mötley Crüe’s John 5, and Jack Black joined the all-star lineup to perform “The Trooper”
entry.content:
The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 induction ceremony took place last night (November 14), but Iron Maiden weren’t there to receive their award because they’re currently on tour. However, St. Vincent, Metallica’s Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo, Rage Against the Machine’s Brad Wilk, Mötley Crüe’s John 5, and Jack Black—who gave the formal induction speech for Iron Maiden right before—assembled in their place to perform the 1983 hit “The Trooper.” Watch the all-star lineup go metal mode below.

During his speech, Black touched on the lifelong influence Iron Maiden have had on metal, how much their music has meant to him, and their steadfast commitment to touring the world. “Has there ever been a band that has rocked this hard for this long? The answer is ‘No,’” Black joked. “In fact, they’re not even here tonight because they’re rocking halfway around the world.”

Iron Maiden has had quite a few lineup changes over their 51-year-long run, and the Rock Hall is honoring their full roster: Steve Harris, Bruce Dickinson, Adrian Smith, Dave Murray, Janick Gers, Paul Di’Anno, Blaze Bayley, Dennis Stratton, Nicko McBrain, and Clive Burr.

entry.title: Panda Bear Remixes Grace Ives’ “Stupid Bitches”
entry.summary: Noah Lennox gives Girlfriend’s standout closer a near-total overhaul
entry.content:
Panda Bear’s Noah Lennox has put his spin on Grace Ives’ “Stupid Bitches,” the standout closer of her new album Girlfriend. Lennox’s version is a near-total overhaul; he cut all new vocals and gave the song’s instrumental a dubby rework. “I'm a huge Panda Bear fan, I am so so happy he did this,” Ives said in press materials. “My new favorite song.” Listen below.

Ives shared Girlfriend, her follow-up to 2022’s Janky Star, in April. Come spring she’ll lend support to Olivia Rodrigo on the European leg of the pop star’s Unraveled Tour.

This year saw Lennox reunite with Sonic Boom’s Pete Kember for A ? of When, their second joint album. He’s also got a live album, PB Band Live 25 at Power Station, on the way next month.

Find out why I named “Stupid Bitches” one of 26 Songs I Want to Hear in the Girls Reboot.

entry.title: Shygirl, Brutalismus 3000, Nirosta Steel Feature on Club Kid Companion EP
entry.summary: Out now, the record includes two covers of Arthur Russell’s “Boy With a Smile”
entry.content:
The soundtrack to Jordan Firstman’s buzzy A24 debut, Club Kid is here. The appropriately club-centric focused EP features Nirosta Steel and Christine and the Queens, who both offer their own takes on avant-garde composer Arthur Russell’s “Boy With a Smile.” Other contributors include Moby, Brutalismus 3000, and Shygirl, who appears as herself in the film. Listen to the songs below.

The A24 feature Club Kid follows a Brooklyn club promoter (Firstman) who lives a hedonistic life until he experiences a rude awakening when he realizes he has a son. The film also stars Cara Delevingne, Miss Benny, Saturn Risin9 as well as involves New York’s nightlife scene, including Amanda Lepeore, Shawn Dickerson, and River Moon.

entry.title: Hayley Williams Brings Out Seu Jorge to Cover David Bowie
entry.summary: The Paramore singer and Life Aquatic star also duetted on “Zissou” in São Paulo
entry.content:
Hayley Williams surprised fans in São Paulo last night by inviting samba legend and all-around Brazilian great Seu Jorge to the stage for a pair of duets. Jorge started with an acoustic, Williams-assisted rendition of his cover of David Bowie’s “Life on Mars?” After that, he backed Williams on her thematically twinned track “Zissou.” Watch clips below.

The latter song, taken from Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party, features a verse in Portuguese that was inspired by Jorge’s musical turns in Wes Anderson’s The Life Aquatic With Steve Zissou OST—including “Life on Mars?”—as Williams told Billboard Brasil in an interview. She recently shared a video for another track from the LP, “Dream Girl in Shibuya.” Jorge continues to release albums of original music, the latest being May’s The Other Side.

entry.title: Drake Updates Take Care With New Song “Hate Sleeping Alone”
entry.summary: Get your brood on with an unearthed cut from the 2011 album
entry.content:
To celebrate the 15th anniversary of his 2011 album Take Care, Drake has dug back in the archives and unearthed a new song from the original sessions, “Hate Sleeping Alone.” Grab a golden chalice, light a candle, and give it a listen below.

Longtime Drake devotees are likely familiar with “Hate Sleeping Alone”—the track has long floated around online via exclusive digital editions, and has been available on Apple Music. The difference is that now, you can listen to it on YouTube and across most other streaming platforms (except Spotify, for reasons unclear).

After a long period of inactivity post-Kendrick beef, Drake dropped a metric ton of music this year. He released three albums in one day in May—Iceman, Habibti, and Maid of Honour—all of which came with accompanying visuals collected as the short film FOMO. Drizzy has also kept busy since, remixing Ella Langley’s monster hit “Choosin’ Texas” with Don Toliver, and linking up with Future, Loe Shimmy, and Travis Scott on last week’s “Ya Hit.”

entry.title: 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now: 2hollis, Armand Hammer, and More
entry.summary: Stream new releases from 2hollis, Ecco2k, Armand Hammer, and U2
entry.content:
With so much good music being released all the time, it can be hard to determine what to listen to first. Every week, Pitchfork offers a run-down of significant new releases available on streaming services. This week’s batch includes new albums from 2hollis, Ecco2k, Armand Hammer, and U2. Subscribe to Pitchfork’s New Music Friday newsletter to get our recommendations in your inbox every week. (All releases featured here are independently selected by our editors. When you buy something through our affiliate links, however, Pitchfork earns an affiliate commission.)

2hollis: Pirouette [Interscope]

Underground-to-mainstream export 2hollis has successfully translated the ragged energy of post-rage into a bona fide pop career. Pirouette meets his skyrocketing profile head-on, going bigger in every possible department. It’s longer, the files are more complicated, the lore is headier, and the sonic profile itself is vast: Emo, pop rock, twee revival, ambient, and choral music all slot into a larger umbrella of pop-EDM. Tying it all together is charismatic Hollis, who matures on sultry, tactile tracks like “Skin” (“Only once I’m under your skin will I feel close enough to you”) and “Sex” (need I elaborate?). Though the album is largely self-produced, Mk.gee notches a writing and production credit on “Human After All.”

Armand Hammer: Snakes and Ladders [Backwoodz]

Armand Hammer, the duo of Elucid and Backwoodz founder billy woods, make their music sound like it is being recited just a foot away from you. That quality is omnipresent on Mercy follow-up Snakes and Ladders. Suffused with political, economic, and technological dread, the album overflows with intimate yarns and moreish imperfections—pianos with no keys, swamps, amd county calls, but also effervescent laughter and Tropical Punch. The production plants you right in the center of it all, within miniature universes where cars rush by, blunted minor chords slink, and haunted melodies loop and reverse.

Ecco2k: Echo [9th]

Despite being an essential Drain Gang member since the 2010s, Ecco2k had only released one solo album, 2019’s E, until now. Carefully crafted over six years, Echo takes the Swedish musician’s world-building to astonishing heights, refining the cloud rap he helped pioneer while escaping its nebulous borders. “Industrial Synth”’s slashes of electric guitar evoke the perkiness of pop rock, “Swimming in Fountains” teems with gurgling, cybernetic IDM synths, and the gliding trip-hop of “Cuban Heel” sounds like an Erika de Casier deep cut. The lyrics tell of molten hot interiors, arrows through the heart, and loveless animals. Echo makes the case for letting the music brew on that hard drive a bit longer. Krill: Secret Language [Exploding in Sound]

Before Krill established their weirdo spin on indie rock in Boston in the early 2010s, the trio grew up in the greater Chicago area before relocating for college. Three albums, one breakup, and a handful of moves later, Krill are back to drumming up new music in the comfort of their hometown. Secret Language, their first full-length in 11 years, takes all the tangled thoughts and pensive observations that are Krill’s bread and butter, and fits them to new musings about parenthood, hobbies, and responsibilities in the modern world. It’s heavy stuff if you let it be, but as always, Krill extend an inviting hand to show you around.

A decade has passed since we last got an album of originals from U2, and they’ve clearly had time on their minds. The impetus for Carnaval de Luz arose after drummer Larry Mullen Jr. injured his neck, bringing into focus the four-person rock ecosystem the band has sustained since the late 1970s. After sessions with Brian Eno and Jacknife Lee materialized into the EPs Days of Ash and Easter Lily, Carnaval De Luz closed the loop on their creative return. It comes complete with a duet featuring the final verse Dolly Parton ever recorded.

Fucked Up’s second album of the year—well, third, depending on your semantic approach to double albums—doubles as the continuation of their Zodiac Cycle and triples as the final installment of their Grass Can Move Stones trilogy. Fans of franchises, concept albums, neoclassical storytelling, and epic hardcore riven with tangents and tributaries will find plenty to tangle with here. When the rapper Aesop Rock and producer Blockhead were growing up, you couldn’t turn on a TV in the tristate area without being inundated with commercials for pristine ski trips to the Poconos. Neither skied nor had equipment, but the promise of a proper ski lodge party always rang as both enticing and empty: like, “must be nice.” Trouble Mountain, the duo’s first joint album since 2021, takes that fantasy and runs away with it, reimagining the Poconos retreat they saw on primetime as a place where, as Aesop says, “You might meet your future spouse or you might have to fight some local ski gangs.” ’Tis the season!

Zsela is getting ready for The Party—that is, her full-length follow-up to 2024’s Big for You and debut for new label Nice Life. The Brooklyn-born, Los Angeles-based singer released lead track “Kinda Guy” last month, and today’s announcement comes with a sultry second single, “Real Romantic.” Listen to that below ahead of the album release on February 19, 2027.

Zsela co-wrote and produced the song with Zack Sekoff and Daniel Memmi; Sekoff worked across the album with Zsela, and the duo brought in contributors including Dijon, Daniel Aged, and Nick Weiss. Zsela will launch the album with a show at L.A.’s 2220 Arts + Archives next week, on November 19.

entry.title: Hear U2’s Posthumous Dolly Parton Duet
entry.summary: “Torn” is the closing track off the band’s new album, Carnaval de Luz
entry.content:
U2 have released their new album Carnaval de Luz, and with it their duet with the late Dolly Parton. The LP’s closing track, “Torn” is supposedly the last song Parton recorded before her death in August. It was co-written with Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, and features steadfast U2 collaborator Daniel Lanois on pedal steel. “Torn apart these loving hearts that beat and break the same,” Parton and Bono sing atop a gentle synth pulse and spare, echoing drums. “We share a house divided and the blood that fills our veins.” Listen below.

Carnaval de Luz marks U2’s first studio album since 2017’s Songs of Experience. It was preceded this year by two surprise EPs—Days of Ash and Easter Lily. “Torn” may be Dolly Parton’s final song, but it won’t be the last Dolly Parton song we ever hear. There apparently exists an unheard recording, titled “My Place in History,” sealed away in a vault at Dollywood, to be unsealed on Parton’s 100th birthday in 2046.

Read Sam Sodomsky’s new review of Carnaval de Luz.

entry.title: Watch Rosalía Perform a Lux Medley at the 2026 Latin Grammys
entry.summary: Her 2025 album is up for seven statuettes tonight
entry.content:
Rosalía opened up the Latin Grammys tonight, offering a medley of songs from her 2025 album Lux. The record picked up seven nominations tonight, and the Catalan singer rose to the occasion wearing a golden gown and surrounded by rows of dancers to perform “La Rumba Del Perdón,” “La Perla,” and “Dios Es Un Stalker.” Watch it below.

It’s already been an exciting month for Rosalía. This week, her role in Wet—a so-far-extremely-mysterious new film from Alma Har’el—was confirmed. Shooting on that is not yet under way. And on November 7, she celebrated Lux’s one-year anniversary by sharing a playlist of songs that inspired the record, including selections from Kate Bush, Yung Lean, Mozart, Caetano Veloso, and more. So far tonight, Rosalía has nabbed one win, for Best Pop Song for “La Perla.”

entry.title: Saba and Pivot Gang Set 2027 North American Tour
entry.summary: The All My Friends Tour is the Chicago rap collective’s first proper run since 2019
entry.content:
Saba and Pivot Gang are bringing all my friends on the road with them next year—no, seriously! The All My Friends Tour, the Chicago rap collective’s first proper run since 2019, kicks off on March 5 in Atlanta, and will feature all five crew members: Saba, MFnMelo, Joseph Chilliams, Frsh Waters, and daedaePIVOT. The run closes out on March 24 with an all-ages show in Los Angeles. Check out all the dates below.

The tour announcement lands just a few weeks after Pivot Gang shared their first new music in two years, “Location."They released their last posse tape, You Can’t Sit With Us, in 2019—it was their final project with former in-house producer Squeak, who died in 2021. Although Pivot Gang as a collective have remained relatively quiet since then, Saba has continued to drop steadily. Last year alone, he shared a solo EP, Coffee!, and a collaborative album with No ID, From the Private Collection of Saba and No ID.

Before they embark on the tour, Pivot Gang will play a hometown show at Thalia Hall on December 19 in honor of John Walt Day. The annual benefit concert is held in memory of Pivot Gang rapper Walter “John Walt” Long Jr., who was murdered in 2017.
